title: Entropy-driven TTL and evidence-sampling policy engine for request artifacts
creator: Aisha Reddy
description: Problem: Customers need retention controls that preserve high-value prompt/response artifacts for longer while keeping total storage and evidence-bundle size bounded for compliance. Current TTLs are route- or tenant-level fixed durations which either over-retain low-value traffic or prematurely purge complex, auditable interactions.
goals: Design and implement a policy engine that attaches adaptive TTLs to request artifacts (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics) based on configurable heuristics (entropy, token-length, error flags, manual tags)
Add evidence-sampling rules to produce compact, auditable bundles for legal/regulatory requests with deterministic selection criteria
Expose policy authoring and a preview/simulator in Console so customers can validate retention outcomes before commit
Make policies tenant-aware and region-aware (data residency) so sampling and TTL assignment respect residency constraints and export requirements
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine accepts JSON policy definitions and evaluates per-request TTL and sampling decision in <= 2ms median on synthetic load
Built-in heuristics: message_entropy, token_count, is_streaming, error_status, customer_tag are supported
Console UI: policy authoring form + live simulator that shows a sampled distribution for a provided sample set (min 1k rows) and exportable CSV
Evidence bundles include provenance metadata (policy_id, evaluated_rules, sampling_seed, resulting_ttl) and pass a deterministic replay test
Retention decisions are honored by purge jobs and by exported evidence bundles across regions (region-aware residency enforced)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Policy model and evaluator library (Go/Rust); integrate into request ingestion path to annotate artifacts with ttl_seconds and evidence_score. Phase 2: Sampling service to periodically build evidence bundles per-tenant and region. Phase 3: Console policy editor + simulator + audit log entries. Phase 4: QA/regression and opt-in beta with 3 pilot customers.
technical_notes: Entropy calculation: use shannon entropy over token distribution of prompt+response; approximate via hashed token buckets for speed
Deterministic sampling: use HMAC(seed=tenant_id + policy_id, input_id) mod 10000 <= threshold to make sampling reproducible across replays
TTL assignment fallback: explicit policy > tag-based override > default route TTL
Store evaluated policy metadata as top-level fields on request artifacts to make purge/replay idempotent
Purge job must consult artifact.ttl_seconds and region tag before deletion; implement dry-run mode for initial rollout
ui_requirements: Console needs a policy authoring editor with: rule builder (if/then blocks), preview pane showing expected retention distribution, ability to mark rules as "fixed" vs "suggested", export policy JSON, and an access-controlled audit trail for changes.
data_residency_considerations: Policies can be flagged as 'residency-strict' (no cross-region evidence export) or 'residency-aware' (evidence sampling happens per-region and bundles are partitioned accordingly). Must integrate with KMS/HSM key selection for bundle encryption per-region.
migration_strategy: For existing tenants: run a simulator over last 30 days of artifacts to produce recommended policy defaults. Offer a one-click apply with a preview and a 14-day shadow mode where new TTLs are annotated but not enforced.
monitoring_and_slos: Track policy-eval latency and % of requests assigned non-default TTL. Alert if eval p95 > 25ms or sampling service backlog grows. Add metrics for evidence-bundle sizes and retention cost delta vs baseline.
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: misconfigured policy leads to over-retention. Mitigation: default deny (honor shorter of existing TTL and computed TTL) and require explicit opt-in for any policy that increases retention above tenant baseline.
Risk: non-deterministic sampling undermines audits. Mitigation: deterministic HMAC-based sampler with seed rotation policy and versioned policy IDs stored with bundles.

Risk: compute overhead at high ingestion rates. Mitigation: allow sampled/approximate heuristics and provide an option for async re-eval in a sidecar that can bump TTLs rather than compute synchronously for every request
rollout_plan: 1) Implement evaluator + offline simulator. 2) Internal dogfood with platform infra tenant. 3) Opt-in beta with 3 pilot customers (SaaS, FinTech, Health). 4) GA with default safe mode (no auto-extension of TTLs) and policy templates for common compliance regimes.
